pairs.difference: A: the asteroid's whole rock face carries an even, fine scratchy grit, with hatched marks along crater rims and the crack. It is sharp at every point and looks like an applied noise layer. Real cards leave large surfaces quiet (neck pillow, submarine hull). B: the bounce house has soft inflated vinyl with small puckered seam ticks and broad wet highlights, close to the pillow's soft seams.
pairs.fix: Smooth matte rock with soft, broad shading. Remove the all-over fine grit and scratch lines. Keep only a few soft-edged craters and leave large calm areas.

pairs.difference: A: the swing ride has soft satin painted metal and plastic, with thin slightly wobbly chains. B: the keyboard has clean matte red plastic, crisp black and white keys and dull grey stand legs. B's detail numbers run over the real range, but that is explained by high-contrast key edges. The real arch in p08 also goes over the range. Neither surface looks wrong for its material.

A: the station's hull, ring and struts are all one satin white ceramic finish. Thin scored panel lines and tiny slots sit on top, with no change of material between parts. B: the bike separates its finishes: glossy red frame, brown saddle, dull dark tyre, thin bright spokes. It has some painterly smear on the car panels, and its out-of-range numbers come from that busy overlap.
pairs.fix: Give the station mixed finishes: dull white painted panels, darker matte joints, brighter bare metal collars with one small sharp highlight. Drop the hairline scored lines.

pairs.difference: A: the scroll has smooth satin paper, a glossy wax seal and a matte ribbon on a shiny blue surface. B: the sheet has soft matte paper with flat ink and quiet wood grain. Both keep marks fine and surfaces calm, as the real cards do. B's low gloss and high highlight share fit its pale paper and give no surface flaw.

B: the rocket's body has an even polished silver sheen with a very crisp small hatch panel, neat tiny rivets and hard red lacquer. All of it is equally sharp, like the added small hardware on generated cameras in the lessons. A: the pool bar mixes soft speckled concrete, matte stool tops, glass and fruit with different finishes. Its speckle is quiet and stays in the wall.
pairs.fix: Rocket in soft painted metal, slightly dull, with broad gentle highlights. Fewer rivets, softly drawn, not etched. Red fins less lacquered than the hull.

pairs.difference: A: the tube has photo-like brushed aluminium with realistic soft creases and a finely ribbed crimp. This is closer to a product photo than the simplified painted metal of the real lamp or fan. B: the vending machine has soft plastic and blurred cans behind a droplet-speckled glass door. It is slightly smeared but sits in the softer real register.
pairs.fix: Paint the tube as simple stylized soft metal: broad clean highlight, two or three smooth dents, no brushed streaks, plain crimp edge.

pairs.difference: A: the observatory stone is putty-soft and uniform with a neat bevel on every block. The dome is the same soft smooth blue, so stone and painted metal differ little in finish; only the telescope is shiny. B: the sand castle has fine sand speckle and crumbly edges, believable as sand, with a shiny contrasting green pail.
pairs.fix: Make the stone drier and more matte with slight variation between blocks. Make the dome a smoother painted metal with one clear soft highlight, clearly different from the stone.

pairs.difference: A is the same rose arch shown among the real cards. Its leaves, petals and wood are crisp but clearly separated. B: the backpack canvas is rubbery and semi-glossy with no weave or stitches, and has slight blotchy paint marks on the green side panel. Metal buckles and leather straps are separated from it. Real cards also omit stitches (glove, pillow), so this is not enough to call B generated.

B: the globe's enamel blue sphere is studded with evenly bright gold beads and stars, and all the gold is the same hot orange lacquer with crisp edges and a slightly gritty shimmer. The decoration is sharper than the form underneath. A: the balloons are soft matte-satin rubber with one gentle highlight each, very quiet and close to the real airbrushed softness. Their low numbers fit bare balloon surfaces.
pairs.fix: Quieter globe: softer painted blue with a broad highlight, fewer stars painted flat into the surface, gold duller and softer with darker aged tones.

pairs.difference: A: the comet has vector-clean flat facets with hard sliver highlights and hairline bright edges, and the tail is a flat gradient. It looks like glossy plastic or an icon, with no ice or rock character. Detail is at the very bottom of the real range. B: the scarf has soft rubbery cloth with no weave, but smooth folds and a matte body, like the real pillow, with a crisp badge.
pairs.fix: Comet rock with softly shaded chipped facets, mixed frosty matte and a few wet ice highlights, slightly irregular edges, and a soft misty tail instead of a flat gradient.

pairs.difference: A: the stems, leaves and pot all have the same lacquered candy gloss with a yellow rim edge and a slightly oversharpened look. Glass bulbs are not much separated from plastic leaves. The table grain is big streaks. B: the book has a matte cover, clean sticker edges and paper page edges, so more finishes per object, though its wood streaks are also big and decorative.
pairs.fix: Leaves matte and soft with no rim glow, pot satin ceramic, only the bulbs glassy. Table grain fine and quiet.

pairs.difference: A: the capsule has crisp brushed-steel gradients, tiny sharp rivets and a hard hairline seam cutting across the red band. Every edge is equally sharp, like the crisp small hardware of generated cards. B: the envelope has soft matte paper with gentle embossed flaps and a glossy printed photo inside. B's over-range numbers come from the tiny village picture, not from a surface fault.
pairs.fix: Capsule in soft painted steel with broad gentle highlights, a few softly drawn rivets, and a subtle seam with no hard hairline. Add some matte areas against the shiny porthole ring.

pattern: Generated cards apply the same sharpness and finish to every surface. They add crisp small hardware (tiny rivets, scored hairlines, beads) or an all-over fine grit, on one lacquered or satin finish. Real cards keep large surfaces soft and quiet, and vary matte and gloss between parts of one object. Out-of-range detail numbers alone are not proof: the real arch in p08 exceeds them too.
